title: Put a group lockout hasp on a disconnect handle and padlock it
instruction: Lock out this switch with the red hasp and your purple padlock: take the hasp out of its holder, open its jaws, close them through the hole in the switch handle, then put the padlock's shackle through a hole in the hasp and snap it shut.
context: In a group lockout the first worker puts a scissor hasp through the switch handle's lock-off hole at OFF and padlocks it, so every later worker can add a lock. The hasp only holds the handle if its jaws are closed through the hole and a padlock keeps the tails from spreading; a hasp that is just closed comes off with a pull.
setup: Positions are from the arm bases (x: cm in front of the bases; y: cm left of the midline between them, which are 61 cm apart; heights above the table top). Switch: a light grey steel enclosure standing on the table (a plain box 12 cm deep, 25 cm wide, 44 cm tall, standing in for the side of a Square D HU361-class heavy-duty safety switch), fixed; its handle wall faces the robot, turned 15 degrees toward the left arm, running from (24.9, -22.4) to (31.3, 1.7). Handle: a 10 cm steel lever (1.1 x 1.6 cm, red 3 cm grip at its end) on a shaft boss 4.5 cm out from the wall, pivot at (25.3, 0.2), 32.3 cm above the table; it points up at OFF (where it starts) and turns 90 degrees toward the right to ON, with an over-centre detent (1.0 N m to push it over). Its 3 mm lock-off tab, 5 cm below the pivot, has an 12 mm square hole that lines up only at OFF with a 12 mm hole in a fixed 3 mm steel ear 3 mm behind it (toward the wall); the holes' centres are 27.3 cm above the table, 26 cm in front of the bases on the midline. Hasp: a Master Lock 420 scissor hasp (two riveted steel jaws, red vinyl-coated tails; 25 mm inside jaw diameter, 11.4 cm long, 4.4 cm wide, six lock holes in 2 columns 2.2 cm apart and 3 rows 1.6 cm apart, holes taken as 8 mm square), closed, standing ring up with its closed tails in the 7 mm slot of a grey holder (a 5 x 2.4 cm block on a column, slot 1.5 cm deep, its floor 12.1 cm above the table) centred at (28.1, 7.2); its flat faces point left and right (turned 15 degrees like the wall), as it will hang on the handle, with the opening side of its jaw ring toward the wall; ring centre 21.5 cm above the table. Padlock: a purple Master Lock 410PRP Zenex safety padlock (thermoplastic body 38 x 19 x 44 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle, 38 mm vertical clearance, 100 g), unlocked with its shackle popped up 16 mm, lying on its 38 x 44 mm side on a grey steel column (1.2 x 3.8 cm, 13.8 cm tall, on a 5 x 6 x 1 cm foot) centred at (15.8, 12.1), its shackle pointing to the right toward the handle. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. Nothing else is on the table. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The score is the highest level reached. 0.25: the hasp is off its holder with its jaws open at least 15 degrees (the tails' bottom corners about 1.8 cm apart) and the centre of its jaw ring within 6 cm of the middle of the two lock-off holes, all at the same moment; a hasp that is knocked over, dropped or just moved scores 0. 0.5: the hasp hangs on the handle with its jaws closed through both lock-off holes: the jaw ring passes through the handle's hole and the ear's hole and the tails are within 5 degrees of shut (their holes lined up). 0.75: also the padlock's short shackle leg passes through a lined-up hole pair of both tails. 1.0: the shackle is snapped shut through such a pair and the after-release check passes. After-release check, done by the reviewer 2 s after both grippers are at least 6 cm from the padlock and from the hasp's ring: (1) pry the tails apart with 0.3 N m about the rivet (6 N on a spring scale hooked through a free tail hole, 5 cm from the rivet) for 1.5 s: pass if the jaws open less than 10 degrees; (2) push the handle toward ON with 1.5 N m (15 N on a spring scale at the lever's tip, 10 cm from the pivot) for 1.5 s: pass if it turns less than 25 degrees. Both must pass; a shut padlock that fails stays at 0.75. Score 0 if at any time before the check the handle turns more than 10 degrees toward ON. Otherwise 0. Angles are read from a photo with a protractor or a phone level.
reset_notes: Unlock the purple padlock with its key, take it out of the hasp and lay it back on its pedestal with its shackle open, shackle toward the switch. Spread the hasp's tails, take it off the handle, close it and stand it back in its holder, tails down in the slot, jaw ring up. Check the handle is at OFF. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints; station arm gains. Published: hasp jaw, length, width and holes; 410 outline. Inferred: hasp plate thickness, hole size and spacing, rivet friction (jaws stay where put up to 0.01 N m), handle size, 1.0 N m detent, shackle travel and spring. Simplified: enclosure is a plain box; lever points up at OFF; box colliders; the jaws do not collide with each other; shackle latches by a rule, no key; check applied after recording. Details in README.
